first_step_test: One rounded head joined to one short pear-shaped body places the squirrel in the center and reserves clear space at the left for the tail and at the chest for the acorn.

source.notes: The first sheet was rejected because its opening head and body shifted. An image-generation edit of panel 2 removed only the ears and tail while preserving the head/body, then that repaired raster cell was registered into the reviewed contact sheet. The original sheet stays private under rejected-progressions.

frames.visible_job: Draw a rounded head connected to a small upright pear body.
frames.instruction: With a black felt tip, draw a round head near the page center and run its lower edge into a short pear-shaped body. Leave room on the left for a large tail and a gap at the chest for one acorn.
adds: joined round head and pear body
introduces: joined round head and pear body

frames.visible_job: Attach one large left-curling tail to the hip and place exactly two pointed ears on the head.
frames.instruction: From the left hip, sweep a broad tail up beside the head and curl its tip inward without touching the face. Attach one small pointed ear to each top side of the head.
adds: two pointed ears and curled left tail
introduces: two pointed ears and curled left tail

frames.visible_job: Place one upright acorn at the chest and wrap exactly two little paws against its sides.
frames.instruction: In the reserved chest gap, draw one upright acorn with a pointed bottom and rounded cap. Bring one small paw from each shoulder to the nut's sides so both paws visibly hold it.
adds: two front paws and one acorn
introduces: two front paws and one acorn

frames.visible_job: Add exactly two eyes, one tiny nose, and a short smile on the fixed head.
frames.instruction: Set two small eyes across the face. Below them, dot a tiny nose and curve a short smile toward the right cheek, keeping the ears and acorn clear.

frames.visible_job: Add one inner tail curve and exactly two short feet beneath the established body.
frames.instruction: Follow the inside of the tail with one broad curved mark, stopping before its curled tip. Under the body, attach two short rounded feet, one on each side of the acorn's point.
adds: tail inner curve and two feet
introduces: tail inner curve and two feet

final_step.visible_job: Fill the existing squirrel and acorn contours with streaky marker color and clarify the existing face.
final_step.instruction: Fill the fixed body and head warm orange, the same curled tail rust, the acorn tan with a dark brown cap, and the belly pale cream. Leave tiny paper streaks, retrace the established edges, and link the existing nose and smile with one tiny mark.
adds: warm orange, rust, tan, brown and cream marker fills

visual_review.first_step_observation: The repaired first saved crop shows the round head attached to the small pear body at their final right-of-center position, with the left side and chest blank. A beginner can place these two connected contours before the tail and acorn.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: I examined the repaired full raster sheet and all six saved crops in order. The same head and pear body carry two ears, one attached left-curled tail, two paws on one acorn, two eyes, one nose and smile, an inner tail line, and two feet. The single acorn and paired features remain countable. No temporary guides or unexplained structural removals remain after replacing the first cell with the image-generated edit.
